questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of shifting cultivation in the order in which they take place:
(A) Moving to a new patch when the soil loses its fertility
(B) Burning the cut vegetation so that the ashes enrich the soil
(C) Growing crops for a few years with simple tools
(D) Cutting down the trees and bushes on a forest patch
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D), (B), (C), (A)
Why: The forest patch is cut (D) and burnt (B), crops are grown for a few years (C), and the farmer moves on when fertility falls (A).
Why not the others: (A) burns before cutting; (B) grows crops before burning; (C) moves on before growing crops.
Key point: This is why it is also called slash-and-burn agriculture.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: India has about 14,500 km of navigable waterways. Which body was set up in 1986 for the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways?
options: A) Inland Waterways Authority of India
C) National Highways Authority of India
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Inland Waterways Authority of India
Why: NCERT notes that the Inland Waterways Authority of India was set up in 1986 for the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways.
Why not the others: The Central Water Commission (B) deals with water resources; NHAI (C) with highways; the Shipping Corporation (D) with ocean shipping.
Key point: Inland waterways are fuel-efficient and environment friendly.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: In 1981, a national committee recommended which areas should be treated as backward hill areas. Which criterion did it use?
options: A) All areas with less than 75 cm of rainfall
B) Hill areas above 600 m outside the tribal sub-plan
C) All districts with a density below 100 persons per sq km
D) Hill areas that border a foreign country
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hill areas above 600 m outside the tribal sub-plan
Why: NCERT notes that the National Committee on the Development of Backward Areas (1981) recommended treating as backward all hill areas above 600 m that were not covered under the tribal sub-plan.
Why not the others: (A) is the definition of dryland farming areas; (C) and (D) are not the committee's criteria.
Key point: Development of hill areas must consider their topography, ecology and social conditions.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.sub_topic: Growth of world population over time
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the growth of the world's population:
(A) It took more than a million years for the world's population to reach one billion.
(B) It took only about 12 years for the population to rise from 5 billion to 6 billion.
(C) Growth speeded up after the spread of agriculture and, later, the Industrial Revolution.
(D) In the 20th century, population grew fastest in the developed countries of Europe.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT: very slow growth for most of history, then faster growth after agriculture, the Industrial Revolution and better medicine.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the fastest growth in the 20th century was in developing countries, where death rates fell while birth rates stayed high. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Expansion of trade, the Industrial Revolution and medical advances all reduced death rates.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Why have countries such as India, China, Indonesia and Brazil developed labour-intensive small-scale manufacturing?
options: A) To provide employment and raise local purchasing power
B) To reduce the need for any raw materials at all
C) To make goods only for export to developed countries
D) Because large-scale industry is banned in these countries
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) To provide employment and raise local purchasing power
Why: NCERT notes that labour-intensive small-scale manufacturing provides employment and raises local purchasing power, which is why these countries have encouraged it.
Why not the others: Small-scale units still need local raw materials (B); they mainly serve local and national markets (C); large-scale industry is not banned (D).
Key point: Small-scale manufacturing uses simple power-driven machines and semi-skilled labour.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Port)
(A) Chennai
(B) Jawaharlal Nehru Port
(C) Marmagao
(D) Haldia

List-II (Feature)
(I) Developed as a subsidiary port to relieve the pressure on Kolkata
(II) At the entrance of the Zuari estuary in Goa, an iron-ore port
(III) At Nhava Sheva, a satellite port to relieve the pressure on Mumbai
(IV) One of the oldest artificial ports of the east coast
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: Chennai is one of the oldest artificial ports on the east coast (IV); Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed to decongest Mumbai (III); Marmagao, at the entrance of the Zuari estuary, handles iron ore (II); Haldia was developed to relieve the pressure on Kolkata (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Chennai and JNPT; (C) swaps JNPT and Marmagao; (D) swaps Marmagao and Haldia.
Key point: JNPT is one of India's largest container ports.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type)
(A) Business process outsourcing (BPO)
(B) Knowledge processing outsourcing (KPO)
(C) Quaternary activities
(D) Quinary activities

List-II (Example or feature)
(I) Decisions taken by senior business executives and top government officials
(II) Research and development, and the handling of information and knowledge
(III) Information-driven work needing highly skilled workers, such as market research
(IV) Routine services such as call centres handled for overseas firms
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: BPO handles routine services such as call centres (IV); KPO handles information-driven knowledge work needing high skills (III); quaternary activities centre on research, development and knowledge (II); quinary activities are decisions by the highest-level policy makers (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps BPO and KPO; (B) swaps KPO and quaternary activities; (C) swaps quaternary and quinary activities.
Key point: KPO lets companies create extra business opportunities.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: Human geography studies the relationship between the physical environment and the cultural environment created by people. Which group consists only of elements of the cultural environment?
options: A) Landforms, soils, climate and natural vegetation
B) Rivers, oceans, wildlife and minerals
C) Houses, villages, roads, industries and ports
D) Mountains, plains, forests and deserts
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Houses, villages, roads, industries and ports
Why: NCERT lists houses, villages, cities, road and rail networks, industries, farms, ports and items of daily use as elements of the cultural landscape created by human activity.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are elements of the physical environment.
Key point: The cultural environment is created by people using the resources of the physical environment.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.sub_topic: Why equatorial forests are thinly populated
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The equatorial rainforests are among the thinly populated regions of the world.
Reason (R): The equatorial rainforests receive very little rainfall during the year.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is true — NCERT notes that areas with very heavy rainfall or extreme and harsh climates have low population. The Reason is false — equatorial forests receive very heavy rainfall throughout the year.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason; (D) needs a false Assertion.
Key point: Thin population in such regions is due to heavy rainfall, dense forests and difficult living conditions.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.sub_topic: The four pillars of human development
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Pillar)
(A) Equity
(B) Sustainability
(C) Productivity
(D) Empowerment

List-II (Meaning)
(I) The power to make choices, through freedom, good governance and people-oriented policies
(II) Human labour productivity, enriched by building people's capabilities
(III) Continuity in the availability of opportunities, so every generation has the same chances
(IV) Equal access to opportunities for everybody, irrespective of gender, race or caste
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: equity is equal access to opportunities (IV); sustainability is the continuity of opportunities across generations (III); productivity is human labour productivity (II); empowerment is having the power to make choices (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps sustainability and productivity; (C) swaps equity and sustainability; (D) swaps productivity and empowerment.
Key point: Development must not be at the cost of future generations' opportunities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question:
Consider the following measures for conserving water:
(A) Reusing treated waste-water in industry and for watering gardens.
(B) Expanding water-intensive crops such as rice and sugarcane in dry areas.
(C) Harvesting rainwater and recharging groundwater.
(D) Developing watersheds by conserving land and water together.
Which of these are measures of water conservation?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: NCERT discusses recycling and reuse of water (A), rainwater harvesting (C) and watershed management (D) as ways of conserving water.
Why not the others: (B) wastes water — water-intensive crops in dry areas cause over-use and waterlogging. Every other option includes (B).
Key point: Conserving water is necessary because demand is rising while supply is limited.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: The first railway line in India, about 34 km long, was opened in 1853 between:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Bombay and Thane
Why: NCERT notes that Indian Railways was introduced in 1853 with a line from Bombay to Thane, covering a distance of 34 km.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the route of the first railway.
Key point: Indian Railways is one of the largest railway systems in the world.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: Opportunities from information and communication technology are spread unevenly — developed countries and urban areas have much better access than developing countries and rural areas. NCERT calls this gap the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Digital divide
Why: NCERT describes the uneven distribution of opportunities from ICT as the digital divide; it exists between countries and within them.
Why not the others: Brain drain (A) is the migration of skilled people; a knowledge economy (B) is one based on information; (D) is not an NCERT term.
Key point: In India, metropolitan cities have better connectivity than rural areas.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about roads in India:
(A) National highways form only about 2 per cent of the total road length but carry about 40 per cent of the road traffic.
(B) State highways are built and maintained by the Central Government.
(C) The Border Roads Organisation builds and maintains roads in the border areas.
(D) District roads are built and maintained by the National Highways Authority of India.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A) and (C) only
Why: (A) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (B) is false — state highways are built and maintained by state governments. (D) is false — district roads are maintained by the Zila Parishad. Every other option includes (B) or (D).
Key point: National highways are the responsibility of the Central Government.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 22
Why: NCERT notes that there are 22 scheduled languages in India.
Why not the others: 18 (B) and 14 (C) were the numbers in earlier years; 24 (D) is not correct.
Key point: India is a land of linguistic diversity, with many languages and dialects grouped into four families.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Before the Green Revolution, the Government of India launched programmes to raise farm output in selected areas by supplying better inputs. They were:
options: A) the Drought Prone Area Programme and the Desert Development Programme
B) the Hill Area Development Programme and the Tribal Sub-Plan
C) Bharat Nirman and Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
D) the IADP and the IAAP (intensive agriculture programmes)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) the IADP and the IAAP (intensive agriculture programmes)
Why: NCERT notes that the Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) and the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP) were launched to improve agriculture before the new seed technology of the mid-1960s.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are target-area programmes of later Plans; (C) are later rural infrastructure schemes.
Key point: The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s with high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: People who move into a new place are called immigrants. What does NCERT call people who move out of a place?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Emigrants
Why: NCERT defines immigrants as migrants who move into a new place and emigrants as migrants who move out of a place.
Why not the others: Refugees (A) flee danger; commuters (B) travel daily and do not change residence; nomads (C) move with their herds.
Key point: Migration can be permanent, temporary or seasonal.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: The area served by a port — from which it receives goods for export and to which it sends imported goods — is called its:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Hinterland
Why: The hinterland is the area served by a port; its size depends on the transport links between the port and the interior.
Why not the others: The foreland (A) is the overseas area a port trades with; a command area (B) is served by an irrigation canal; a catchment (C) drains into a river.
Key point: Kandla's hinterland covers much of north-western India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: The Human Development Report, which ranks countries by their HDI score, has been published every year since 1990 by the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) UN Development Programme (UNDP)
Why: NCERT notes that the UNDP has published the Human Development Report every year since 1990, ranking countries by their performance in health, education and access to resources.
Why not the others: The World Bank (B) and IMF (C) focus on finance and development lending; the WTO (D) deals with trade rules.
Key point: Mahbub-ul-Haq and Amartya Sen worked on the early reports.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: In a year, a region recorded 30,000 births and 12,000 deaths. During the same year, 5,000 people moved in and 8,000 moved out. What was the actual growth of its population?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 15,000
Given: births 30,000; deaths 12,000; in-migrants 5,000; out-migrants 8,000.
Step 1: Natural growth = births − deaths = 18,000.
Step 2: Actual growth = natural growth + in-migrants − out-migrants = 18,000 + 5,000 − 8,000 = 15,000.
Common mistake: stopping at natural growth (18,000, option A), or adding both migration figures (31,000) or reversing them (21,000, option C).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Industries that make products such as bread and biscuits, tea, soaps, toiletries, paper and televisions, which are used directly by people, are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Consumer goods industries
Why: NCERT classifies industries by product: consumer goods industries make goods consumed directly by people, while basic industries make goods used to make other goods.
Why not the others: Basic (A) and heavy (C) industries supply other industries; mineral-based (D) is a classification by raw material.
Key point: Iron and steel is a basic industry; a television factory makes consumer goods.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: When ore lies deep below the surface, underground (shaft) mining has to be used. Why does NCERT call it risky?
options: A) Poisonous gases, fires, floods and caving in
B) It can only be carried out during the dry winter season
C) It always leaves the land surface completely flooded
D) It can never be mechanised, so all work is done by hand
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Poisonous gases, fires, floods and caving in
Why: NCERT notes that underground mining needs special lifts, drills, haulage vehicles and ventilation, and is risky because of poisonous gases, fires, floods and caving in, which lead to fatal accidents.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not the risks NCERT names; shaft mines are highly mechanised.
Key point: Open-cast mining, used for minerals near the surface, is cheaper and safer.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.sub_topic: Language families by number of speakers
questions.question:
Arrange the following language families of India in descending order of their share of speakers:
(A) Austric
(B) Dravidian
(C) Indo-European
(D) Sino-Tibetan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (B), (A), (D)
Why: NCERT's figures: Indo-European (Aryan) about 73 per cent (C); Dravidian about 20 per cent (B); Austric about 1.38 per cent (A); Sino-Tibetan about 0.85 per cent (D).
Why not the others: (A) puts Sino-Tibetan above Austric; (C) puts Dravidian above Indo-European; (D) puts Austric above Dravidian.
Key point: The two smaller families are spoken mainly in the north-east and in tribal areas of central and eastern India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: NCERT identifies three important regions of pastoral nomadism. Which of the following is one of them?
options: A) The Prairies of North America and the Pampas and Velds of the south
B) The Amazon and Congo basins of the equatorial rainforest zone
C) From North Africa's Atlantic coast east across Arabia to Mongolia
D) North-western Europe and the north-eastern parts of the USA
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) From North Africa's Atlantic coast east across Arabia to Mongolia
Why: NCERT's three regions are: the core region from the Atlantic shores of North Africa across the Arabian peninsula into Mongolia and Central China; the tundra region of Eurasia; and south-western Africa and Madagascar.
Why not the others: The grasslands in (A) have extensive grain farming and ranching; (B) has gathering and shifting cultivation; (D) has mixed and dairy farming.
Key point: The number of pastoral nomads is falling as governments settle them and political boundaries limit their movement.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.sub_topic: Hierarchy of urban places by size
questions.question:
Arrange the following urban places from the smallest to the largest by population, using NCERT's terms:
(A) Mega city — more than 5 million
(B) Town — less than 1 lakh
(C) Metropolitan city — 1 million to 5 million
(D) City — 1 lakh to 1 million
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: NCERT calls an urban centre with more than one lakh people a city; cities of one to five million are metropolitan cities, and those above five million are mega cities.
Why not the others: (B) puts the city below the town; (C) puts the metropolitan city below the city; (D) puts the mega city below the metropolitan city.
Key point: Greater Mumbai and Delhi are India's largest urban agglomerations.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: According to NCERT, the main sources of air pollution are:
options: A) organic farming, composting and tree plantation
B) solar panels, wind turbines and hydro power
C) combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries
D) rainwater harvesting, recycling and watershed works
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries
Why: NCERT names the combustion of fossil fuels, mining and industries as the main sources of air pollution; they release oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, hydrocarbons, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, lead and asbestos.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are clean or conservation practices.
Key point: Air pollution affects the respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, which group lists the factors that attract tourists to a place?
options: A) Cheap land, cheap labour, raw materials and power
B) Climate, landscape, history and art, culture and economy
C) Large markets, ports, government policy and capital
D) Fertile soils, irrigation and high crop yields
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Climate, landscape, history and art, culture and economy
Why: NCERT names climate, landscape, history and art, and culture and economy as the main tourist attractions.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are factors of industrial location; (D) relates to agriculture.
Key point: Tourism has become the world's single largest tertiary activity in jobs and revenue.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: Which group consists only of towns that NCERT classifies as industrial towns?
options: A) Kandla, Kochi, Kozhikode and Visakhapatnam
B) Jamshedpur, Bhilai, Modinagar and Salem
C) Mathura, Amritsar, Madurai and Puri
D) Chandigarh, Bhopal, Shillong and Gandhinagar
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Jamshedpur, Bhilai, Modinagar and Salem
Why: NCERT lists Mumbai, Salem, Coimbatore, Modinagar, Jamshedpur, Hugli and Bhilai among industrial towns.
Why not the others: (A) are transport (port) towns; (C) are religious and cultural towns; (D) are administrative towns.
Key point: A town may perform several functions but is classed by its dominant one.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Suez Canal is a sea-level canal without locks.
Reason (R): The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and shortens the route between Europe and Asia.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true — NCERT describes the Suez Canal, built in 1869 in Egypt between Port Said and Port Suez, as a sea-level canal without locks that links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. But the seas it links and the distance it saves do not explain why it has no locks.
Why not the others: (A) treats the Reason as the cause; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: The Panama Canal, by contrast, has a six-lock system.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.sub_topic: Definition of human geography by Vidal de la Blache
questions.question: Which geographer described human geography as a "conception resulting from a more synthetic knowledge of the physical laws governing our earth and of the relations between the living beings which inhabit it"?
options: C) Paul Vidal de la Blache
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Paul Vidal de la Blache
Why: NCERT quotes this definition from Paul Vidal de la Blache, a leading figure of the French school associated with possibilism.
Why not the others: Ratzel (A) called it the synthetic study of human societies and the earth's surface; Semple (B) spoke of the changing relationship between the unresting man and the unstable earth; Griffith Taylor (D) proposed neo-determinism.
Key point: All three definitions stress the relationship between people and the earth.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Noise pollution is location-specific.
Reason (R): Its intensity declines as the distance from the source — industrial areas, arterial roads, airports — increases.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. NCERT explains that noise pollution is location-specific because its intensity falls with distance from the source — this explains the Assertion.
Why not the others: (B) would need the Reason to be unrelated; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Noise pollution is hazardous along highways, near airports and in industrial areas.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about high-technology industries:
(A) They depend on intensive research and development to make products of an advanced scientific character.
(B) Professional (white collar) workers make up a large share of the workforce.
(C) Robotics, computer-aided design and electronic controls are common in them.
(D) Their landscape is marked by massive assembly halls, factories and storage yards.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT's description of high-tech industry as the latest generation of manufacturing.
Why not the others: (D) is false — NCERT says the high-tech landscape has neatly spaced, low, modern, dispersed office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: High-tech industries cluster in technopolis such as Silicon Valley.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: Ports that handle both bulk cargo and general cargo in large volumes, as most of the world's great ports do, are classified as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Comprehensive ports
Why: NCERT classifies ports by cargo: industrial ports specialise in bulk cargo such as grain, sugar, ore, oil and chemicals; commercial ports handle general cargo; comprehensive ports handle both in large volumes.
Why not the others: Industrial (B) and commercial (C) ports specialise; packet stations (D) carry passengers and mail.
Key point: Ports are also classified by location and by specialised function.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Which important inland waterway of Eastern Europe rises in the Black Forest, flows eastwards through many countries, and carries wheat, maize, timber and machinery?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The Danube
Why: NCERT describes the Danube as an important inland waterway serving Eastern Europe; it rises in the Black Forest and flows eastwards through many countries.
Why not the others: The Rhine (A) flows north to Rotterdam; the Volga (B) flows into the Caspian Sea; the Seine (C) is not described in NCERT as a major waterway.
Key point: The Rhine waterway is navigable from Rotterdam to Basel.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: In the Human Development Index, the health of a country's people is measured by:
options: A) the number of hospitals per lakh people
B) the infant mortality rate alone
C) government spending on health care
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) life expectancy at birth
Why: NCERT notes that the indicator chosen to assess health is life expectancy at birth — a higher life expectancy means a greater chance of living a long and healthy life.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are useful health data, but they are not the HDI's health indicator.
Key point: Education and access to resources are the HDI's other two dimensions.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Pulses are an important source of protein in Indian food. Which two does NCERT name as the main pulses grown in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Gram and tur (arhar)
Why: NCERT notes that gram and tur (arhar) are the main pulses grown in India.
Why not the others: Soyabean, groundnut, mustard and sesamum (B, D) are oilseeds; ragi and jowar (C) are millets.
Key point: Pulses are leguminous crops that raise soil fertility by fixing nitrogen.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: Which country specialises in growing flowers and horticultural crops, especially tulips, which are flown to all the major cities of Europe?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The Netherlands
Why: NCERT gives the Netherlands as the example of a country specialising in flowers and horticultural crops, especially tulips.
Why not the others: Denmark (A) is known for cooperative dairy farming; New Zealand (B) for dairying and ranching; southern Italy (C) for Mediterranean agriculture.
Key point: Market gardening is practised in densely populated industrial districts with high-income markets.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, over-withdrawal of groundwater has increased the concentration of fluoride in the groundwater of parts of:
options: B) Kerala, Goa and coastal Karnataka
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Rajasthan and Maharashtra
Why: NCERT links over-withdrawal of groundwater with higher fluoride levels in parts of Rajasthan and Maharashtra.
Why not the others: West Bengal and Bihar (A) are linked with arsenic; NCERT does not name (B) or (D).
Key point: Excess fluoride in drinking water damages teeth and bones.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about ports:
(A) Inland ports, such as Manchester and Memphis, are located away from the sea coast and are linked with the sea by a river or canal.
(B) A country has a favourable balance of trade when the value of its exports is more than the value of its imports.
(C) Ports of call are ports that handle only the export of mineral oil.
(D) Out ports are deep-water ports built away from the actual port, serving the parent port, as Piraeus serves Athens.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (C) is false — ports of call, such as Aden and Honolulu, are stopping points on main sea routes where ships refuel and take on supplies; oil-handling ports are oil ports. Every other option includes (C).
Key point: Kolkata is an inland port on the Hugli.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Ocean route)
(A) Northern Atlantic Sea Route
(B) Mediterranean–Indian Ocean Sea Route
(C) North Pacific Sea Route
(D) South Pacific Sea Route

List-II (What it links)
(I) Western Europe and North America with Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands, via the Panama Canal
(II) The west coast of North America with ports such as Yokohama, Shanghai and Singapore
(III) Western Europe with East Africa, South Asia and Australia, through the Suez Canal
(IV) North-eastern USA with north-western Europe
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: The Northern Atlantic route links north-eastern USA and north-western Europe (IV); the Mediterranean–Indian Ocean route passes through the Suez Canal (III); the North Pacific route links North America's west coast with Asia (II); the South Pacific route links Europe and North America with Australia and New Zealand via Panama (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps the first two routes; (C) swaps the Mediterranean and North Pacific routes; (D) swaps the two Pacific routes.
Key point: Honolulu is an important port on the South Pacific route.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: Which of the following is a target-area programme, as described in NCERT?
options: A) The Command Area Development Programme
B) The Small Farmers Development Agency
C) The Marginal Farmers Development Agency
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Command Area Development Programme
Why: NCERT gives the Command Area Development Programme, the Drought Prone Area Programme, the Desert Development Programme and the Hill Area Development Programme as target-area programmes.
Why not the others: SFDA (B) and MFDA (C) are target-group programmes; the PDS (D) is a food distribution scheme.
Key point: Target-area planning aims to reduce regional imbalances.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: The period 1951–1981 in India's demographic history is called the period of population explosion. Why?
options: A) The birth rate rose sharply above 60 per thousand
B) Large numbers of people migrated into India from other continents
C) Both birth and death rates rose together in these decades
D) The death rate fell rapidly while the birth rate stayed high
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The death rate fell rapidly while the birth rate stayed high
Why: NCERT notes that after Independence, development activities and better health care lowered the mortality rate quickly while fertility remained high, giving a very high growth rate.
Why not the others: The birth rate did not rise to such levels (A); migration from Bangladesh, Nepal and Pakistan added to growth but was not the main cause (B); the death rate fell, not rose (C).
Key point: After 1981 the growth rate began to fall slowly.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.sub_topic: Water needed to irrigate a field
questions.question: A farmer wants to give a 2-hectare field one irrigation equal to 50 mm of water. What volume of water is needed? (1 hectare = 10,000 m²)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 1,000 m³
Given: area = 2 ha = 20,000 m²; depth = 50 mm = 0.05 m.
Step 1: Volume = area × depth.
Step 2: 20,000 × 0.05 = 1,000 m³ (10 lakh litres).
Common mistake: forgetting to convert hectares to square metres, or millimetres to metres (100 or 10,000 m³, options A and C).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, which areas have a very large proportion of their workers in "other services" (the secondary and tertiary sectors)?
options: D) Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry
Why: NCERT notes that highly urbanised areas such as Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have a very large proportion of workers in other services.
Why not the others: Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland (A) have large shares of cultivators; Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand (B), Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal (D) have high proportions of agricultural labourers.
Key point: Occupational structure reflects the level of urbanisation and industrialisation.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Types of farming by source of moisture
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type of farming)
(A) Protective irrigation
(B) Productive irrigation
(C) Dryland farming
(D) Wetland farming

List-II (Feature)
(I) Rainfall in the rainy season exceeds the soil-moisture needs of plants
(II) Areas with less than 75 cm of annual rainfall, growing hardy crops such as ragi and bajra
(III) Provides enough soil moisture to achieve high productivity
(IV) Protects crops from the adverse effects of soil-moisture deficiency
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: protective irrigation saves crops from moisture deficiency (IV); productive irrigation gives enough moisture for high productivity (III); dryland farming is in areas with less than 75 cm of rain (II); wetland farming is where rainfall exceeds the soil-moisture needs (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps protective and productive irrigation; (B) swaps dryland and wetland farming; (D) swaps productive irrigation and dryland farming.
Key point: Wetland areas may face floods and soil erosion.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.sub_topic: Mineral belt of the Chotanagpur plateau
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

India's minerals are not spread evenly. NCERT groups most of them into three broad belts, with some minerals found outside them.

The North-Eastern Plateau Region covers the Chotanagpur plateau of Jharkhand, the Odisha plateau, West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh. The South-Western Plateau Region extends over Karnataka, Goa and the contiguous uplands of Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The North-Western Region extends along the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat; its minerals are associated with the Dharwar system of rocks.

Outside these belts, the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten in both its eastern and western parts. Assam has mineral oil deposits, and oil resources are also found off the coast near Mumbai (Mumbai High).

Question: The Chotanagpur plateau, rich in a variety of minerals such as iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica, belongs to which mineral belt?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The North-Eastern Plateau Region
Why: The passage places the Chotanagpur plateau of Jharkhand in the North-Eastern Plateau Region, which NCERT describes as having a variety of minerals — iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.
Why not the others: The North-Western Region (A) lies along the Aravallis; the South-Western Region (C) covers Karnataka and Goa; the Himalayan belt (D) lies in the north.
Key point: This belt is the base of India's iron and steel industry.

Outside these belts, the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten in both its eastern and western parts. Assam has mineral oil deposits, and oil resources are also found off the coast near Mumbai (Mumbai High).

Question: Which mineral belt is rich in ferrous metals and bauxite, has high-grade iron ore, manganese and limestone, but lacks coal deposits except for the lignite of Neyveli?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) The South-Western Plateau Region
Why: NCERT describes the South-Western Plateau Region in these terms; it does not have coal except the Neyveli lignite of Tamil Nadu.
Why not the others: The North-Eastern Plateau (A) has most of India's coal; the North-Western Region (B) is known for copper, zinc and building stones; the Himalayan belt (D) has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten.
Key point: Goa in this belt is known for iron ore.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.sub_topic: Major minerals of the North-Western Region
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

India's minerals are not spread evenly. NCERT groups most of them into three broad belts, with some minerals found outside them.

The North-Eastern Plateau Region covers the Chotanagpur plateau of Jharkhand, the Odisha plateau, West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh. The North-Western Region extends along the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat; its minerals are associated with the Dharwar system of rocks.

Outside these belts, the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten in both its eastern and western parts. Assam has mineral oil deposits, and oil resources are also found off the coast near Mumbai (Mumbai High).

Question: In the North-Western Region, along the Aravallis, which two minerals does NCERT name as the major ones, associated with the Dharwar system of rocks?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Copper and zinc
Why: NCERT states that copper and zinc are the major minerals of the North-Western Region, associated with the Dharwar system.
Why not the others: Coal and iron ore (A) and bauxite and mica (B) are typical of the North-Eastern Plateau; monazite and thorium (C) occur in Kerala.
Key point: Rajasthan's copper deposits are in Jhunjhunu and Alwar districts.

Outside these belts, the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten in both its eastern and western parts. Assam has mineral oil deposits, and oil resources are also found off the coast near Mumbai (Mumbai High).

Question: Rajasthan, in the North-Western Region, is rich in building stones. Which group does NCERT name?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Sandstone, granite and marble
Why: NCERT notes that Rajasthan is rich in building stones — sandstone, granite and marble; gypsum and Fuller's earth deposits are also extensive, and dolomite and limestone supply the cement industry.
Why not the others: Monazite and ilmenite (B) are beach-sand minerals of Kerala and Tamil Nadu; bauxite (C) is mostly in Odisha and Jharkhand; coal (D) is mainly in the North-Eastern Plateau.
Key point: Gujarat in this region is known for its petroleum deposits, and both states produce salt.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.sub_topic: Minerals of the South-Western belt and others
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

India's minerals are not spread evenly. NCERT groups most of them into three broad belts, with some minerals found outside them.

The North-Eastern Plateau Region covers the Chotanagpur plateau of Jharkhand, the Odisha plateau, West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh. The South-Western Plateau Region extends over Karnataka, Goa and the contiguous uplands of Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The North-Western Region extends along the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat; its minerals are associated with the Dharwar system of rocks.

Outside these belts, the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten in both its eastern and western parts. Assam has mineral oil deposits, and oil resources are also found off the coast near Mumbai (Mumbai High).

Question: Which of the following pairs of a place and a mineral is correctly matched, according to NCERT?
options: B) The Himalayan belt — the lignite of Neyveli
D) The Odisha plateau — offshore petroleum
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Kerala — monazite and thorium
Why: NCERT notes that Kerala, in the South-Western Plateau Region, has deposits of monazite and thorium, along with bauxite clay.
Why not the others: Goa (A) is known for iron ore, not coal; Neyveli (B) is in Tamil Nadu; offshore petroleum (D) is at Mumbai High, not in Odisha.
Key point: Monazite is the main source of thorium for India's nuclear programme.
